metaDescription: SecuEdge protects SaaS companies, startups and IT firms from supply chain attacks, credential-based intrusions and C2 callbacks — keeping customer data and source code secure.

hero.headline: Protect Your Platform, Your Code, Your Customers
hero.sub: SolarWinds cost an average of $12M per affected organisation. Kaseya's one exposed VSA server became ransomware in 1,500 downstream businesses. The source of trust in your supply chain is your network perimeter.

challenges.title: Supply Chain & Trusted Update Compromise
challenges.desc: APT29's SolarWinds attack embedded a backdoor in a digitally-signed software update. 18,000 organisations installed it — including DHS and the Department of Energy — and went undetected for nine months.

challenges.title: Credential Theft via Infostealer Malware
challenges.desc: The Snowflake campaign used credentials harvested by infostealer malware to access 165+ customer data warehouses without MFA. No exploit was required — just stolen passwords.

challenges.title: Exposed Management Consoles
challenges.desc: REvil exploited an authentication bypass in Kaseya's VSA management console exposed directly to the internet. The result: malicious updates pushed to 60 MSPs and 1,500 downstream businesses.

challenges.title: CI/CD Pipeline Secret Exfiltration
challenges.desc: API keys and GitHub credentials embedded in CI/CD pipelines are high-value targets. Compromise of a single credential set can cascade to every client repository a development firm touches.

challenges.title: DDoS as Cover for Simultaneous Intrusion
challenges.desc: Volumetric DDoS attacks on SaaS platforms and API endpoints are used to distract security teams while a concurrent intrusion exploits weakened perimeter defences.

challenges.title: Developer Remote Access Without Boundaries
challenges.desc: Developers working from home, client sites and co-working spaces access production infrastructure from unmanaged devices on untrusted networks — expanding the credential risk surface enormously.

threats.title: Trusted Update Channel Weaponisation
threats.desc: When a vendor's software update mechanism becomes an attack vector, no endpoint security catches the payload — it arrives pre-trusted. The only detectable signal is the C2 beacon the backdoor makes after installation.

threats.title: Credential-Only Access to Cloud Data
threats.desc: Without MFA on cloud data platforms, stolen credentials are all an attacker needs. ShinyHunters and similar groups systematically target Snowflake, Salesforce and similar platforms with infostealer-harvested credentials.

threats.title: Management Console Exploitation
threats.desc: Any management interface exposed directly to the internet is a persistent target. Kaseya VSA, Atlassian, RMM tools and similar platforms have all been exploited when left internet-facing without VPN protection.

threats.title: Source Code and IP Exfiltration
threats.desc: Game source code, proprietary algorithms, client codebases and internal tooling represent years of investment. Bulk exfiltration goes unnoticed on flat networks without traffic monitoring.

approach.title: Never Expose Management Ports Publicly
approach.desc: Every management console, admin panel, VSA, RMM tool and internal dashboard sits behind SecuEdge's VPN — accessible only via authenticated tunnel. Kaseya-style exploitation requires internet exposure; remove the exposure, remove the risk.

approach.title: DNS Blocking Catches the Inevitable C2 Beacon
approach.desc: Even a successfully installed backdoor (SolarWinds model) needs to phone home. SecuEdge's malware and newly-registered domain blocking categories intercept C2 beacons at the DNS layer before data leaves.

approach.title: Force Cloud Platform Access Through Authenticated Networks
approach.desc: Restrict Snowflake, GitHub, Salesforce and similar cloud platforms to connections originating from corporate IP ranges via SecuEdge VPN — infostealer credentials from personal devices cannot authenticate.

approach.title: Segment Dev, Staging and Production
approach.desc: Firewall rules enforce that development networks cannot initiate connections to production systems without explicit policy. CI/CD pipelines run in isolated zones; a compromised workstation cannot reach production directly.

capabilities.title: VPN-Protected Management Access
capabilities.desc: Every internal management console, admin dashboard, RMM tool and CI/CD system sits behind SecuEdge VPN with certificate and MFA authentication — zero internet-exposed management surfaces.

capabilities.title: DNS & Content Category Blocking
capabilities.desc: Block malware distribution domains, known C2 infrastructure and newly-registered domains across all networks — intercepting the C2 beacons that supply-chain backdoors depend on to receive instructions.

capabilities.title: Firewall Network Segmentation
capabilities.desc: Dev, staging, production and client environments on separate VLANs with explicit firewall rules. A compromised developer workstation cannot pivot to production databases or client repositories.

capabilities.title: Bandwidth Monitoring & Exfil Detection
capabilities.desc: Establish baselines for normal outbound traffic from code repositories and internal servers — bulk downloads and unusual data transfers trigger real-time alerts before exfiltration completes.

capabilities.title: Egress Firewall (Default-Deny)
capabilities.desc: Outbound connections to uncategorised, newly-registered or unlisted destinations are blocked by default — internal systems can only reach explicitly whitelisted business endpoints.

capabilities.title: Load Balancing & DDoS Resilience
capabilities.desc: Dual-WAN load balancing distributes ingress traffic and keeps SaaS platforms and API endpoints available when one link is targeted by volumetric DDoS — with bandwidth management to rate-limit attack traffic.

process.title: Exposure Audit
process.desc: Identify every management console, admin panel and internal tool exposed directly to the internet — the Kaseya attack surface. Map cloud platform access and review which networks can reach production.

process.title: Secure & Segment
process.desc: Move all management access behind VPN with MFA, implement dev/staging/production VLAN segmentation, enforce egress filtering and enable DNS blocking.

process.title: Monitor & Baseline
process.desc: Establish normal outbound traffic patterns for code repositories and cloud platforms; configure alerts for bulk transfers; review DNS query logs for C2 beacon patterns weekly.

faqs.q: How does SecuEdge help against supply chain attacks like SolarWinds?
faqs.a: SecuEdge cannot prevent a compromised vendor update from installing — but it can catch the next required step: the C2 callback. SUNBURST called out to avsvmcloud.com for instructions. SecuEdge's DNS category blocking intercepts that callback at the network layer before any commands are received or data leaves.

faqs.q: Our developers access production from home. How does SecuEdge handle that?
faqs.a: All production access routes through SecuEdge VPN with certificate and MFA authentication. Remote developers get the same encrypted, authenticated tunnel whether they're at home, a client site or a co-working space — and access is limited to the specific production systems their role requires.

faqs.q: We use Snowflake, GitHub and Salesforce for customers. Can SecuEdge protect cloud platform access?
faqs.a: Yes. SecuEdge firewall rules restrict outbound connections to these platforms to IP ranges associated with your corporate VPN. Staff accessing these platforms from personal devices or non-VPN networks get blocked at the egress layer — infostealer credentials from unmanaged devices cannot authenticate.

faqs.q: Can SecuEdge protect against DDoS on our SaaS platform?
faqs.a: SecuEdge's dual-WAN load balancing distributes ingress traffic across multiple links and bandwidth management rate-limits traffic spikes that match DDoS patterns. For volumetric DDoS at scale, SecuEdge works alongside upstream ISP scrubbing services.

cta.headline: Secure Your Platform From Supply Chain to Production
cta.sub: Put every management console behind VPN, block C2 beacons at the DNS layer and segment dev from production — before the next Kaseya or Snowflake campaign finds your environment.
